claim_formal: (W = grt solution space with Ihara bracket) ≅ Lie_Q⟨e_3,e_5,e_7,…⟩ as graded Lie algebras, e_{2k+1} ↦ σ_{2k+1}, also after weight completion

quote_A.text: the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra is freely generated by one element in every odd weight at least three

quote_B.text: We prove the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture

notes: Prefix: grt is a pre-named object, so none; the theorem/Lean literally read ∃ σ (∃ graded iso e), so ∃ is an alternative. Existence (Ihara) and freeness (Brown/Willwacher) parts were prior; the new content is exhaustion, hence full_only_with_prior_results.

claim_formal: ∀ f ∈ Z[x] irreducible, deg f = d ≥ 4, with ρ_f(p^{d-2}) < p^{d-2} ∀p: #{n ≤ X : f(n) is (d-2)-power-free} = c_f X + o_f(X), c_f = ∏_p(1-ρ_f(p^{d-2})/p^{d-2}) > 0

quote_A.text: every irreducible integer quartic with no fixed prime-square divisor takes squarefree values with the predicted positive Euler-product density

quote_B.text: Proves the squarefree-values conjecture for irreducible integer quartics with no fixed prime-square divisor

notes: Headline = quartic case (k=2, d=4) of the squarefree-values conjecture, which is posed for all degrees, hence O5/restricted_range; the paper also proves (d-2)-power-free density for 4≤d≤8 and, with Browning (d≥9), all d≥4 (that is the Lean allDegrees statement, which contains the quartic headline). Alternative reading: the (d-2)-power-free problem for all d≥4 as the posed problem → O1.

claim_formal: ∀ complex CM abelian variety A, ∀ p ≥ 0, ∀ α ∈ H^{2p}(A,Q) ∩ H^{p,p}(A): ∃ Z ∈ CH^p(A)_Q with cl_B(Z) = α

quote_A.text: every rational Hodge class on such a variety is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes

quote_B.text: We prove the rational Hodge conjecture for complex abelian varieties with complex multiplication

notes: Matrix could also be read as M1 (surjectivity of cl_B as a property, prefix ∀). Corollaries via Milne: Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties. Other manuscripts: HC/GHC on a K3 quadratic locus via algebraic Kuga–Satake; HC on self-powers of split Weil sixfolds and of abelian varieties of dim ≤5 with imaginary-quadratic action; HC for powers of abelian-cover Jacobians and diagonal complete intersections; a conditional Kuga–Satake reduction.

claim_formal: ∀ finite quiver Q, ∀ dimension/framing vectors, ∀ commuting flavor torus F, ∀ regular stability ν: H_F^*(X_ν) ≅ C[Y_f^ν] as graded R-algebras (both coefficient maps surjective with equal kernels)

quote_A.text: They therefore induce a canonical isomorphism of graded $R$-algebras

quote_B.text: We prove the equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for arbitrary finite quivers, including loops and multiple arrows

notes: Conjecture as formulated in DK25 Conjecture 2.1; the regularity hypothesis (semistable = stable, free action) is part of the stated setting.

claim_formal: ∀ connected compact Kähler manifold X: X special → π_1(X) is virtually abelian

quote_A.text: the fundamental group of every special compact Kähler manifold is virtually abelian

quote_B.text: resolving Campana's abelianity conjecture in all dimensions

notes: Corollaries: Kodaira-dimension-zero case, Conjecture S, holomorphic convexity. Other manuscripts: an independent proof (priority Cao–Deng–Hacon–Păun) of class-≤2 virtually nilpotent linear monodromy for special quasi-projective varieties; a conditional orbifold abelianity theorem for order-two root orbifolds of fourfolds.

claim_formal: ∀ domain G ⊂ Ĉ (nonempty connected open): ∃ circle domain V, ∃ conformal equivalence f: G → V

quote_A.text: Every nonempty connected open set $G\subset\Chat$ is conformally equivalent to a circle domain.

quote_B.text: resolving Koebe's circle-domain conjecture positively

notes: Second manuscript: circle domains with conformally removable boundary are rigid (removability→rigidity direction of He–Schramm; the converse is false by Rajala); its Lean theorem removability_implies_rigidity is also present.

claim_formal: ∃ absolute a_* ∈ (0,1/2), C_* < ∞ ∀ Lipschitz v: R²→S¹ with Lip(v) ≤ 1, ∀ 0<ε<a_*, ∀ f ∈ S(R²): ‖H^ε_{v,a_*} f‖_2 ≤ C_* ‖f‖_2 (hence strong and weak (2,2) for the principal value)

quote_A.text: There are absolute constants \(a_*\in(0,1/2)\) and \(C_*<\infty\) such that every Lipschitz field

quote_B.text: This gives an affirmative answer to Stein's weak-$`(2,2)`$ conjecture.

notes: Scale restricted to length ~ 1/Lip(v), which is the scale in Stein's formulation (Lacey–Li Conj. 1.5), so O1 not O5; restricted_range marks the short-scale restriction in the headline. 'ineffective' = constants not made explicit.

claim_formal: ∃ real homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial p (with direction e) such that ¬∃ finite affine semidefinite lift of the closed hyperbolicity cone K(p,e)

quote_A.text: There exists a real homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial whose closed hyperbolicity cone has no finite semidefinite lift.

quote_B.text: This disproves the Projected Lax Conjecture and hence the generalized Lax conjecture.

notes: Lean formalizes the companion explicit degree-20, 23-variable cone that is not spectrahedral (disproves only the generalized Lax conjecture); that cone does admit a semidefinite lift (third manuscript), so the Lean does not cover the Projected Lax disproof.

claim_formal: ω(C) ≤ 9/4, i.e. ∀ε>0: n×n complex matrices multiply in O_ε(n^{9/4+ε}) operations

quote_A.text: We prove that the exponent of matrix multiplication over the complex numbers is at most 9/4.

quote_B.text: Dupont et al. report $\omega<2.371177$ by optimizing this combination-loss framework

notes: Other manuscripts: ω<2.258, α>0.465, ω(1,0.709,1)<2.092 in char 0; ω<2.371054886006746 over every fixed field. Lean contains all of these, including complex_omega_le_nine_quarters.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ ε ∈ [0,1/2], ∀ f: {±1}^n → {±1}: I(f(X);Y) ≤ 1 − h_2(ε), with equality for (signed) dictators

quote_A.text: the universal bound in bits is \[ I_2(f(X);Y)\le\frac{\psi(\rho)}{L}=1-h_2(\varepsilon). \] This is the Courtade--Kumar conjecture.

quote_B.text: The Boolean specialization resolves the Courtade–Kumar conjecture

notes: Main theorem is a stronger soft-channel contraction I(T_ρu) ≤ ψ(|ρ|ψ^{-1}(I(u))); second manuscript proves the Hellinger conjecture (ABCJN) for all biases, which also implies Courtade–Kumar. M9 because the bound is attained by dictators.

claim_formal: ∀ C > 0 ∃ n ∃ nonconstant total f: {0,1}^n → {0,1} with bs(f) > C·s(f)^2 (indeed bs(f)/s(f)^2 ≥ 2^d/(4(d+2)^2) for each d)

quote_A.text: constructing nonconstant total Boolean functions whose block sensitivity grows faster than any constant multiple of sensitivity squared

quote_B.text: We disprove the quadratic strengthening of the Sensitivity Conjecture

notes: Could also be coded M8 (quantitative separation bs ≥ s^α, α>2). The quadratic bound bs ≤ s^2 was suggested by Nisan–Szegedy; Lean states the quantitative family version.

claim_formal: ∃ C^∞ volume-preserving diffeomorphism T of T^3 ∃ real f ∈ L^2_0: {f∘T^n : n ∈ Z} is an orthonormal basis of L^2_0(T^3) (simple Lebesgue spectrum)

quote_A.text: There exist a $C^\infty$ volume-preserving diffeomorphism $T\colon\T^3\to\T^3$ and a real function $f\in L^2_0(\T^3,\mu)$

quote_B.text: We solve the probability-preserving form of Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem in smooth dynamics.

notes: The paper distinguishes this probability-preserving form from the historical real-line question attributed to Banach by Ulam; if the posed problem is taken to be that original form, outcome would be O5. Smoothness is extra strength, not a restriction.

claim_formal: ∃ compact X ⊂ R^9 (X = {uu^T : u ∈ S^3} in trace-one Sym_4 with Frobenius metric) such that X cannot be covered by 10 subsets of diameter < diam X = √2

quote_A.text: has diameter $\sqrt2$ and cannot be covered by ten subsets of diameter strictly less than $\sqrt2$

quote_B.text: Theorem~\ref{thm:main} improves this dimension bound using the full compact image of projective space rather than a finite configuration.

notes: Borsuk's conjecture was already disproved (Kahn–Kalai); the open target is the least counterexample dimension (previously 63/64). Dimension 9 improves the record without determining it (tie-break 7 → P4/O7). Corollary: counterexamples in every d ≥ 9.

claim_formal: ∀ natural unit interval graph G on [n]: χ_G(X;q) = Σ_{σ ∈ D_G^0} q^{ginv_G(σ)} e_{θ_G(σ)}(X); in particular every e-coefficient of χ_G lies in N[q]

quote_A.text: the chromatic quasisymmetric function of every natural unit interval graph is elementary-positive over $`\mathbb N[q]`$

quote_B.text: This resolves the elementary-positivity part of the Shareshian–Wachs conjecture.

notes: Only the e-positivity part of Shareshian–Wachs is settled (no e-unimodality claim); coded O1 since e-positivity is the stated conjecture, O5 is the alternative. Corollary on Young permutation modules in Hessenberg cohomology.

claim_formal: ∃ C > 0 ∀ n ∀ simple graph G on n vertices: E(G) partitions into ≤ Cn cycles and single edges

quote_A.text: There is an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that, for every finite simple undirected graph \(G\) with \(n\) vertices

quote_B.text: This resolves the Erdős–Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture positively.

notes: Inner ∃ (the partition) is part of the bounded quantity; the full prefix would be ∃∀∃. Linear order is optimal (trees) but C is not determined, so M8 not M9. Corollary: Eulerian graphs decompose into O(n) cycles.

claim_formal: ∀ regular local ring (R,m), ∀ nonzero f.g. R-modules M,N: ℓ(M⊗N) < ∞ ∧ dim M + dim N = dim R → χ^R(M,N) > 0

quote_A.text: If $\length_R(M\otimes_R N)<\infty$ and $\dim_R M+\dim_R N=d$, then \[ \chi^R(M,N)>0. \]

quote_B.text: We prove Serre's positivity conjecture, including ramified mixed characteristic.

notes: Remaining case was ramified mixed characteristic (equal char/unramified by Serre, nonnegativity by Gabber). Paper notes a same-scope unverified public claim (Editan, Dec 2025).

quote_A.text: the tensor square of the corresponding irreducible complex representation of the symmetric group contains every irreducible representation of that group

quote_B.text: This proves Saxl's conjecture.

notes: Companion manuscript proves the Pak–Panova–Vallejo tensor square conjecture: ∀ n ∉ {2,4,9} ∃ λ ⊢ n ∀ ν: g(λ,λ,ν) > 0 (Lean universal_tensor_square); corollary for unipotent characters of GL_n(F_q). Both Lean statements present; saxl_conjecture matches the headline.

claim_formal: ∀ β > 1: Var F_n(β) ~ c_β n^{1/3} with c_β > 0, and (F_n − E F_n)/sd(F_n) ⇒ ν_β (nondegenerate, moment-determined) as n → ∞

quote_A.text: We also prove that its variance divided by n1/3 converges to a finite positive constant.

quote_B.text: confirming the predicted n1/6 standard-deviation scale

notes: Problem is a physics prediction (Crisanti–Paladin–Sommers–Vulpiani, Parisi–Rizzo) of the n^{1/6} scale rather than a named math conjecture; P1 vs P2 is uncertain. The limiting law goes beyond the prediction. Companion manuscript: sd = n^{1/6+o(1)}. Corollaries: SK–Curie–Weiss fluctuations, disorder-chaos bounds.

claim_formal: ∀ d (regular d-ary, d ≥ 2, or Poisson(d) GW tree, d > 1), ∀ admissible λ, symmetric 3-state channel (and ferromagnetic 4-state, λ ≥ 0): reconstruction ⇔ dλ^2 > 1 (non-reconstruction at equality)

quote_A.text: reconstruction occurs if and only if \[ d\lambda^2>1, \] with $d=b$ in the regular case. At every admissible equality $d\lambda^2=1$, there is non-reconstruction.

quote_B.text: This resolves the all-degree three-state regular-tree prediction.

notes: The reconstruction direction dλ^2>1 is classical Kesten–Stigum; the new content is non-reconstruction at and below the threshold. Both Lean comparators formalize only the supercritical (Kesten–Stigum) direction, so 'weaker' (one direction, and the known one). Corollary: exact weak-recovery threshold for the 3-community SBM. Also a four-state L3-capacity criterion on bounded-degree trees. restricted_range = q ∈ {3,4} only (KS is not tight for large q).

claim_formal: ∀ π ∈ Aut(D_T, ≤_T), ∀ a ∈ D_T: π(a) = a

quote_A.text: Every order automorphism of the full Turing-degree structure is the identity

quote_B.text: resolving the rigidity conjecture for the Turing degrees positively

notes: Matrix ambiguity: could be M4 (no nontrivial automorphism exists; prefix then none) or M7 (Aut(D_T) = {id}). Coded as stated in Lean (∀π ∀a). Uses Slaman–Woodin's arithmetic representation theorem as external input.

claim_formal: ∃ group G: G infinite ∧ finitely presented ∧ simple ∧ amenable

quote_A.text: There exists an infinite finitely presented simple amenable group.

quote_B.text: giving a positive answer to the finite-presentation existence question for simple amenable groups

notes: Question recorded by Button (2010) and Juschenko–Monod (2013); not a named conjecture or numbered list item.

claim_formal: ∀ q, R, J, Δ > 0 ∃ C ∀ finite induced Λ ⊂ Z^2, ∀ admissible H on Λ with unique ground state Ω and gap ≥ Δ, ∀ A ⊆ Λ: S_Ω(A) ≤ C |∂_Λ A|

quote_A.text: there is a finite constant $C=C(q,R,J,\Delta)$ with the following property

quote_B.text: We prove an entropy area law for the unique ground state of a finite-range Hamiltonian on any finite induced subgraph of the square lattice.

notes: Low-confidence B: the area-law conjecture for gapped ground states is usually posed in all dimensions ≥ 2; this settles the 2D square-lattice case (O5, restricted_range). If the 2D area law is taken as its own posed problem, O1. Second manuscript: polynomial-bond-dimension PEPS approximation on L×L squares (PEPS conjecture for that class).

claim_formal: ∃ κ_0 > 0 ∀ finite two-player game G with ω*(G) = v < 1, ∀ 0 < δ < 1−v, ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ finite-dim entangled strategy S for G^k: Pr[W_k ≥ ⌈(v+δ)k⌉] ≤ exp(−κ_0 δ^5 k / (1 + log |A||B|))

quote_A.text: \Pr\!\left[W_k\ge\lceil(v+\delta)k\rceil\right] \le \exp\!\left(-\frac{\kappa_0\delta^5} {1+\log d}\,k\right).

quote_B.text: Proves exponential threshold repetition for every finite two-player one-round game

notes: Lean uses δ^13 instead of δ^5, so it is weaker than the paper's rate. Problem is an open question (threshold parallel repetition for entangled games), not a named conjecture. Uses Song's conditioning estimate as input.

claim_formal: ∀ ε > 0 ∃ δ > 0 ∀ Hilbert space H, ∀ unital von Neumann algebras M, N ⊆ B(H): d(M,N) < δ → ∃ unitary u: uMu* = N ∧ ‖u − I‖ < ε

quote_A.text: there is a unitary $u\in\B(H)$ satisfying \[ uMu^*=N,\qquad \norm{u-I_H}<\eps. \]

quote_B.text: This resolves the strong Kadison–Kastler conjecture.

notes: Other manuscripts give negative answers to neighbouring questions: one-sided near inclusions without small spatial embeddings (CCSSWW question), and close norm-separable C*-algebras not unitarily conjugate (separable C* spatial form of Kadison–Kastler).

claim_formal: ∀ separable nuclear C*-algebras A, B: T(A) ≅ T(B) as topological cones → A⊗W⊗K ≅ B⊗W⊗K (realizing the given cone map)

quote_A.text: the canonical topological cone of all extended lower-semicontinuous tracial weights determines a separable nuclear C∗-algebra after tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators

quote_B.text: answering Robert's trace-cone classification question positively

notes: Matrix: a classification-by-invariant theorem (invariant is complete); M6 chosen, M5 (iso ⇔ cone iso, one direction trivial) is the alternative. Lean only formalizes auxiliary lemmas (closed ideals ↔ idempotent extended traces), not the classification, hence 'different'.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p, ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ t ∈ Z: π_t L_{K(n)} S_p^∧ is a finitely generated Z_p-module

quote_A.text: the homotopy groups of the $`K(n)`$-local sphere are finitely generated ℤp-modules in every integer degree, for every prime p and positive height n

quote_B.text: This answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey–Strickland.

notes: Equivalent form: same for L_{K(n)}F for every finite p-local spectrum F.

claim_formal: ∀ Hilbert space H, ∀ A ∈ B(H), ∀ m, ∀ P ∈ M_m(C)[z]: ‖P[A]‖ ≤ 2 sup_{z ∈ W(A)} ‖P(z)‖, and 2 cannot be decreased

quote_A.text: proving the sharp constant-two numerical-range inequality for every bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space and every matrix-valued polynomial

quote_B.text: We resolve the complete Crouzeix conjecture

notes: Implies the scalar Crouzeix conjecture. M9 because the constant 2 is shown sharp (uniformly over n, m, d). Second manuscript gives a direct matrix proof; structural results on optimal similarity (κ ≤ 2) and a common positive boundary representation. Lean CrouzeixHilbert / CompleteCrouzeix main include sharpness.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ κ ≤ 0, ∀ complete simply connected (M^n,g) with Sec ≤ κ, ∀ measurable E with vol(E) < ∞, P(E) < ∞: P(E) ≥ I_{√−κ}(vol(E)) (equal-volume model ball)

quote_A.text: every finite-volume set of finite ambient perimeter has perimeter at least that of the equal-volume ball in curvature κ

quote_B.text: We resolve the generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture in every dimension.

notes: M9 vs M8: the comparison is sharp (model balls attain it) and the κ=0 equality case is classified; coded M9. Lean formalizes the companion sharp integral filling theorem in proper CAT(0) spaces (plus coefficient optimality), which gives only the Euclidean (κ=0) case for d ≥ 3: a secondary result, so 'different'. Corollaries: Faber–Krahn and Saint-Venant comparisons.

claim_formal: ∀ m ≥ 2, ∀ closed connected M^m, ∀ minimal immersion F: M → S^{m+1} with F(M) not totally geodesic: Vol(M, F*g) ≥ a_m = min_k Vol(C_{k,m−k}) (attained by a Clifford product)

quote_A.text: a closed connected minimal immersion with non-totally-geodesic image has volume at least the smallest m-dimensional minimal Clifford product

quote_B.text: We prove the Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces of unit round spheres

notes: Also Problem 31 in Yau's 1994 problem collection (P3 is a defensible alternative); coded P1 since both the paper and summary call it the Solomon–Yau conjecture (Ge–Li Conj. 1.12(ii)).

claim_formal: ∀^∞ k ∃ complete smooth metric g_k on R^3 with Ric ≥ 0: h_k(R^3, g_k) ≥ (k+2)^2 > (k+1)^2 = h_k(R^3, g_E)

quote_A.text: all sufficiently large integers k admit a complete smooth metric on ℝ3 with nonnegative Ricci curvature, asymptotic volume ratio v, and at least $`c(k+1)^2`$ linearly independent real harmonic functions of pointwise growth at most k

quote_B.text: This answers Yau's integer-degree dimension comparison question negatively in dimension three

notes: Lean MainClaim formalizes the companion manuscript's single counterexample (some even n ≥ 8, some k ≥ 2), not the R^3 all-large-k family: 'different' (it still refutes the comparison). Threshold k_0(v,c) not explicit, hence ∀^∞. Summary calls it Yau's 'proposed' bound; treated as a question (P2).

claim_formal: ∃ ρ ∈ C_c^∞(R^3) probability density (√ρ ∈ C_c^∞) such that the 3-marginal Coulomb Kantorovich minimum E(μ) is finite and attained, Monge infimum = E(μ), but ∀ measure-preserving Borel T_2, T_3: ∫ c(x,T_2x,T_3x) dμ > E(μ)

quote_A.text: every pair of Borel maps \(T_2,T_3:\R^3\to\R^3\) satisfying \((T_2)_\#\mu=(T_3)_\#\mu=\mu\) obeys

quote_B.text: The question is whether absolute continuity of \(\mu\), together with \(\E(\mu)<\infty\), guarantees an optimal Monge plan. We give a counterexample with additional regularity.

notes: Refutes the Monge (co-motion) ansatz for three-marginal Coulomb transport; extended to all inverse-power Riesz costs in every d ≥ 2.
